title: Easy Rice Recipes
excerpt: Find easy rice recipes for weeknights and Sunday supper—how to cook rice by type, chicken and rice dinners, casseroles, biryani, and rice noodles, all gathered in one cozy guide.

contentHtml:
A pot of rice on the stove is one of the simplest comforts in a home kitchen. Fluffy white rice, fragrant jasmine, nutty brown rice, or a full chicken-and-rice supper can all start with the same quiet confidence. This guide gathers Grandma Recipe’s best rice recipes—how-to methods by rice type, easy rice dinners, casseroles, bowls, and biryani—so you can choose a path and cook with confidence.

Use this page as your starting point. Each section below links to tested recipes with clear steps, everyday ingredients, and that cozy, from-scratch flavor we love for weeknights and Sundays alike.

How to Use This Rice Recipes Guide

Start with what you need tonight:

  • Need a dependable side? Begin with How to Cook Rice, then choose jasmine, basmati, or brown.
  • Cooking a full plate? Jump to chicken over rice, kielbasa and rice, or rice and beans.
  • Want oven comfort? Open a chicken broccoli rice casserole or rice stuffing.
  • Craving a special rice night? Try biryani or crispy rice with spicy tuna.

If you are new to stovetop rice, start with How to Cook Rice. For fragrant weeknight rice, How to Cook Jasmine Rice is a lovely next step.

Rice Cooking Basics

A few steady habits keep rice recipes fluffy instead of sticky or scorched:

  • Rinse when the recipe calls for it — rinsing removes extra surface starch for lighter grains.
  • Use the right water ratio for the rice type you are cooking.
  • Keep the lid closed while the rice simmers so steam can finish the work.
  • Rest off the heat before fluffing so moisture settles through the pot.
  • Fluff gently with a fork rather than stirring hard, which can mash the grains.

Our full method lives in How to Cook Rice, with dedicated guides for the most-loved rice varieties.

How to Cook Rice by Type

Different grains need slightly different care. These how-to guides walk through each one clearly:

  • How to Cook Rice — the foundational stovetop method for fluffy white rice.
  • How to Cook Jasmine Rice — fragrant, soft grains for curries, bowls, and everyday sides.
  • How to Cook Basmati Rice — long, separate grains with a delicate aroma.
  • How to Cook Brown Rice — nuttier brown rice with a sturdy, wholesome bite.
  • Jasmine Brown Rice — jasmine brown rice when you want fragrance and heartiness together.

Easy Rice Dinners

Rice is more than a side. These rice recipes turn grains into the heart of supper.

  • Chicken Over Rice — seasoned chicken over a generous bed of rice.
  • Slow Cooker Chicken and Rice — slow cooker chicken and rice for hands-off evenings.
  • Kielbasa and Rice — sausage and rice for a quick skillet-style comfort plate.
  • Rice and Beans — rice and beans for a simple, satisfying supper.
  • Lamb Over Rice — lamb over rice when you want a richer dinner bowl.
  • Pho and Rice — a cozy pairing of pho flavors with rice on the side.

Rice Casseroles and Sides

When the oven can help, rice becomes casserole comfort or a holiday-ready side.

  • Chicken Broccoli Rice Casserole — chicken, broccoli, and rice under a golden topping.
  • Rice Stuffing — rice stuffing for roast dinners and festive tables.

Make-ahead tip: many rice casseroles reheat well with a splash of broth to restore moisture.

Biryani and Special Rice

Some rice recipes are celebration food—layered spices, fragrant steam, and a table that feels a little more special.

  • Homemade Biryani — homemade biryani with inviting spice and tender layers.
  • Mutton Biryani — mutton biryani for a hearty feast plate.
  • Goat Biryani — goat biryani with deep, savory flavor.
  • Crispy Rice with Spicy Tuna — crispy rice topped with spicy tuna for a fun appetizer-style bite.

Rice Noodles

Rice also shows up as noodles—another easy path for weeknight bowls and stir-fries.

  • Flat Rice Noodles — stir-fried flat rice noodles with vegetables.
  • Rice Stick Noodles — rice stick noodles for quick savory plates.

What to Serve with Rice

  • Roast chicken, baked fish, beans, or a simple vegetable curry
  • Steamed greens, roasted carrots, or a crisp salad
  • A pat of butter, fresh herbs, or a squeeze of lemon for plain rice
  • Leftover rice turned into next-day bowls or fried-rice style skillet meals

Make Ahead, Storage, and Leftovers

  • Cool rice promptly and refrigerate within 2 hours in shallow containers.
  • Use refrigerated rice within 3 to 4 days.
  • Freeze cooled portions in airtight containers for up to about 1 month for best texture.
  • Reheat until steaming hot, adding a splash of water to restore moisture.

FAQs About Rice Recipes

Do I always need to rinse rice?

For many white rice recipes, rinsing helps remove excess starch. Follow the linked method for each rice type—start with How to Cook Rice.

Why is my rice mushy?

Too much water, too much stirring, or skipping the rest can soften the grains. Measure carefully and keep the lid on while it cooks.

Which rice should I cook first?

Begin with How to Cook Rice or How to Cook Jasmine Rice. Once that feels easy, try brown rice or a full dinner like Chicken Over Rice.

Can I make rice ahead for busy nights?

Yes. Cook a batch, cool it quickly, refrigerate, and reheat with a little water. It also works well under leftover chicken, beans, or vegetables.

What is the difference between jasmine and basmati?

Jasmine is soft and fragrant; basmati cooks into longer, more separate grains. Compare How to Cook Jasmine Rice and How to Cook Basmati Rice to see which you prefer.

Final Thoughts

Good rice recipes do not need complicated equipment—just the right grain, a steady simmer, and a little patience at the end. Bookmark this guide, pick a cluster, and cook one pot at a time. Before long you will have fluffy sides, easy rice dinners, and a few special-occasion dishes ready for the family table.
